items.title: Chico Freeman interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 13, 2001
items.q: Saxophone players — from Chu Berry to Lester Young to Coleman Hawkins to Ben Webster, Ornette Coleman, Charlie Parker, Eric Dolphy.

ctx.x: Yes, and they took Lester Young down in the basement and played all these records of Coleman Hawkins and asked him — and Lester replied, “If you want him then you hire him.” So you know Thelonious Monk, his style, and you look at all the great — McCoy Tyner, Thelonious Monk, Bud Powell, you know as far as pianists go. Bill Evans. You know you listen to these pianists. Wynton Kelly. Red Garland. They sound different.
They have their own sounds. Andrew Hill. Saxophone players — from Chu Berry to Lester Young to Coleman Hawkins to Ben Webster, Ornette Coleman, Charlie Parker, Eric Dolphy.
I’m wondering if, because of so much education going on with jazz now that we’ve dissected everything they do and there is so much for people to copy that that’s how they end up.
